newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh stockmarket launch delayed until September.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh stockmarket launch delayed until September.

text.p: The launch of Kazakhstan's stock market has been delayed until September because the government has not yet decided the size of stakes in quoted companies to be offered to portfolio investors, a senior official told Reuters.

"The government planned to define this in April... which means it had to say... what stake in what company must be sold on the stock exchange in 1997," said Grigory Marchenko, Chairman of the National Securities Commission.
Marchenko has said previously his commission was planning to hold pilot auctions of stakes in a number of companies this May.

Earlier this year the government published a list of about 60 big companies, representing large banks, oil and gas groups, and communications and other major sectors of the economy, in which minority stakes would be offered to portfolio investors.
The authorities of the resource-rich Central Asian state view the selected companies as potential "blue chips" and the core of the future shares market.
Marchenko said he was hopeful the government would announce the names of the first companies and the stakes to be offered in them to portfolio investors this week.

"July and August are traditionally quiet months with low business activity, so we plan to start the active work of the stock market in September. The plan of the functioning of this market remains unchanged," he said.
Marchenko said the list approved by the government would include large enterprises of interest to Western investment banks and smaller ones more likely to be handled by local brokers and dealers.
"I think, this list will include 10-15 companies, with five or six very large ones which will have to undergo classical listing procedures," he said.

Another reason for the delay in the stock market's start was that companies designated by the government as "blue chips" had to bring their accounts into line with international standards and undergo an international audit, Marchenko said.
The central depository and stock exchange will prepare the necessary legal documents only by the end of July, he added.

He said the tender to select banks which would handle initial private offers was close to an end. Salomon Brothers, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, ABN AMRO Bank and Daewoo Securities are competing for the right to handle these offers.
